# Cybou

> Cybou is an intelligent, reproducible personal Linux distribution built on NixOS 26.05 and KDE Plasma 6 Wayland. Created by Stanislav Saveliev.

## Overview
Cybou follows a strict two-stage philosophy: **Build a trustworthy body first, then grow the cognitive mind.**

- **Visual & Technical Body (v0.1)**: Immutable NixOS Flakes base, atomic generation rollbacks, custom KDE Plasma 6 Wayland desktop theme ("Cybou Horizon"), zero telemetry, WCAG AA contrast compliance.
- **On-Device Cognition (v0.2+)**: Local SLM/LLM system services executing strictly on local NPU/GPU hardware. Natural-language system state introspection, log diagnostic assistance, and local vector context with 100% privacy and zero cloud dependencies.

## Technical Details & Contact
- Base System: NixOS 26.05 stable locked via `flake.lock`.
- Desktop Environment: KDE Plasma 6 (Wayland) + SDDM greeter.
- Security & Telemetry: 100% zero remote telemetry. No external API keys required.
- Official Contact: info@cybou.fr
- Official Website: https://cybou.fr
- GitHub: https://github.com/cybou-fr/CYBOU

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

### Q: What is Cybou?
A: Cybou is an intelligent personal Linux distribution created by Stanislav Saveliev. Built on NixOS 26.05 and KDE Plasma 6 Wayland, it provides a calm, mathematically reproducible desktop paired with on-device local AI assistance.

### Q: Why is Cybou called a "Smarter Linux"?
A: Cybou integrates local SLMs/LLMs directly into the system layer. It offers natural language introspection of NixOS generation changes, build error diagnostics, and local vector context with 100% privacy and zero cloud telemetry.

### Q: Does Cybou require cloud services or send telemetry?
A: No. Cybou strictly enforces 100% Zero Telemetry. No accounts, API keys, or external servers are required. All AI models run locally on GPU/NPU in sandboxed systemd containers.

### Q: How does Cybou guarantee system stability?
A: Through declarative NixOS Flakes (flake.lock) and atomic generation rollbacks. If any package update fails or breaks, you can instantly select a previous working generation at boot time.

### Q: What open-source licenses apply?
A: Cybou code and Nix expressions are licensed under MIT. Original visual assets (wallpapers, desktop themes, SVGs) are licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0. Copyright (c) 2026 Stanislav Saveliev.
